name: Avus
notes: The Automobil-Verkehrs- und Übungsstraße — a public motor road through the Grunewald forest in south-west Berlin, linking Charlottenburg with Nikolassee, begun in 1913 and opened as a racing circuit in 1921. Two straights of some nine kilometres each, joined at either end, made it less a circuit than a speed trial run in a loop. For 1937 the northern hairpin was rebuilt as a brick-paved wall of banking angled at 43.6 degrees, taken flat out and quickly nicknamed the Wall of Death: run wide and you left over the top. Hermann Lang won that May's race for Mercedes at an average of around 260 km/h with peaks near 380 km/h, the fastest road race ever run to that point. Driven counter-clockwise.
author: Legion
